name: Dihydrotestosterone (DHT)

lead: DHT is a hormone made from testosterone that shapes male genital development and puberty changes, and it is also the hormone behind male-pattern baldness. Forum users apply DHT gel hoping for a more masculine face, beard or penis size.
DHT gel has been studied in older men with low testosterone and used in boys with micropenis, but no trial has tested it for looks in people without a hormonal disorder.

paras: DHT binds the androgen receptor more strongly than testosterone does and cannot turn into estrogen. Applied as a gel, it is absorbed through the skin and raises DHT in the blood.

Users and a forum-cited study describe suppression of the body's own testosterone with DHT gel. Androgens can cause acne and mood changes, and their effect on adolescent growth is unstudied. DHT gel is not an approved US product.

lead: Dihydrotestosterone (DHT, 5alpha-dihydrotestosterone, androstanolone) is an endogenous androgen made from testosterone by the enzyme 5alpha-reductase, mainly in tissues such as the prostate, skin and hair follicles. It binds the androgen receptor more strongly than testosterone and cannot be converted to estrogen by aromatase [1]. It drives development of the male external genitalia in the fetus and, at puberty, facial and body hair, and it is implicated in male-pattern hair loss and prostate enlargement [1][2][3].

In looksmaxxing communities, DHT is discussed in two ways: as something to lower, through 5alpha-reductase inhibitors such as finasteride and dutasteride for hair loss, and as something to apply, in homemade or compounded topical DHT gels that some users say can enhance facial bone masculinisation during puberty, beard growth or penile size [4][5]. A prescription DHT gel was studied in a phase 2 trial in older men with low testosterone, and topical DHT has been used clinically in boys with micropenis [6][7]. No published trial has tested topical DHT for facial structure in people without an endocrine disorder.
infobox: Topical gel (investigational/clinical use outside US); endogenous
About 2-fold higher affinity than testosterone, slower dissociation (per Grokipedia) [1]
Androgens are controlled substances in many countries; DHT gel is not an FDA-approved US product

paras: DHT circulates at roughly 5 to 10 percent of the level of testosterone and is formed mainly at the site of action [1]. In male fetuses, high local DHT concentrations are needed to form the penis, scrotum and prostate; a sterile review of micropenis notes that conversion of testosterone to DHT and its action at the androgen receptor are necessary for normal penile development [6]. At puberty, DHT promotes facial and body hair, sebum production and voice deepening; in genetically susceptible adults it shortens the growth phase of scalp hair follicles, leading to miniaturisation [1][2][8]. Reviews describe different follicles responding in opposite ways: beard follicles are stimulated and scalp follicles in androgenetic alopecia are suppressed [8][2]. A classic 1974 study of 5alpha-reductase deficiency in men described an inherited form of pseudohermaphroditism due to impaired DHT formation [9].

DHT gel has been tested for treating symptoms of low testosterone in men aged 55 to 80 (phase 2, 128 participants) [7] and an earlier-stage study measured its effects on prostate tissue in healthy men [10]. Hormonal therapy for micropenis may include intramuscular or topical testosterone or topical DHT [6]. Imaging with a fluorinated DHT analogue has been tested in prostate cancer [11].

Because DHT mediates androgenetic alopecia, finasteride and dutasteride, which block 5alpha-reductase, are used for hair loss. Systematic reviews and randomized trials report efficacy for these and for topical finasteride [2][12][13][14][15]. Clascoterone, a topical androgen receptor inhibitor competing with DHT, is approved for acne [16].

A registered phase 2 study in 128 men aged 55 to 80 tested DHT gel for symptoms of late-onset hypogonadism [7]. A phase 1/2 study of 31 healthy men examined DHT effects on prostate tissue [10]. No study has tested topical DHT for facial bone growth, beard growth or penile size in healthy people, and none has examined it in adolescents with typical development. A rugby-player trial and a 12-week randomized trial examined whether creatine changes DHT; these concern creatine, not DHT use [17][18].

A looksmax.org poster who cites a study reports that two years of DHT gel was associated with an 84 percent fall in testosterone alongside a roughly sevenfold rise in DHT, and that users on the forum take this as evidence that the gel suppresses the natural axis [19].

Reported effects of exogenous androgens as a class include suppression of the body's own testosterone production, acne and mood changes. Forum members report emotional effects and, as noted above, suppression with DHT gel [19][20]. A key theoretical concern in adolescents is that androgens advance bone maturation and can shorten final height, although users in the community argue that DHT, not aromatizable, avoids estrogen effects; no study has examined this [4]. Because DHT promotes prostate growth, 5alpha-reductase inhibitors are used in prostate enlargement, and the Prostate Cancer Prevention Trial of finasteride examined prostate cancer rates [21]. Grokipedia states that elevated DHT has not been linked to higher prostate cancer risk in most studies [1].

Threads on looksmax.org have promoted DHT gel as a "pubertymaxing" tool, arguing that DHT is the main driver of brow ridge, jaw, cheekbone and voice development, is two to three times more androgenic than testosterone and does not aromatize, and that applying it during puberty could enhance masculine bone structure [4]. The author noted the topic is "often mocked" on the forum [4]. Other threads ask whether it works for penile length or girth, mandible growth, or after puberty, with reports of both claimed growth and doubt that the gel works for penile growth [5][19][22][23][24][25]. Some users pair it with topical finasteride for hair, which commenters question [5]. On T Nation, DHT mainly appears in lab panels for men on testosterone therapy, with high DHT linked by users to acne and libido questions [26][27].

lore.intro: Topical DHT gel is a recurring topic on looksmax.org, in guides, success claims and skeptical threads about face, beard, penis and puberty [4][19][22][23].
